name: Pacific West Coast US (California · Oregon · Washington)

language.script_notes: Spanish signage common in California, especially in agricultural Central Valley and southern California.
false_friends: British Columbia, Canada (same coastal conifer forest)

road_furniture.guardrail_type: Common on winding coastal/mountain roads (e.g. Highway 1).
road_furniture.line_paint: Botts' dots (raised round non-reflective lane markers) historically used instead of painted lane lines on California freeways are a state-specific tell where visible.
road_furniture.curb_style: Concrete curbs in dense coastal cities; open shoulders on rural coastal highways.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Dense overhead wiring in coastal California towns.

architecture.roof_style: Low-pitch roofs on mid-century California suburban stock; steeper roofs further north in wetter Oregon/Washington to shed rain.
architecture.roof_material: Red clay tile roofing common on Spanish/Mission-revival houses in California.
architecture.wall_construction: Stucco construction very common in California (earthquake-country building style); wood-frame siding more common further north in Oregon/Washington.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Warm stucco tones and Mission-revival white/terracotta in California; muted greens/greys against dense evergreen backdrops further north.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Spanish Mission-revival architecture with red tile roofs (California); redwood-country cabins and lodges; Pacific Northwest craftsman-style wood houses; tech-campus modern architecture in the Bay Area; vineyard architecture in Napa/Sonoma.

nature.vegetation: Towering coast redwoods in northern California/southern Oregon are a near-unique regional tell; Douglas fir, western hemlock and red cedar dominate further north in Oregon/Washington; golden dry grass hills and oak woodland in inland/central California; vineyards in Napa/Sonoma/Central Coast.
nature.terrain: A dramatic, often cliff-lined Pacific coastline; the Coast Ranges and Cascades running the length of the region; the flat agricultural Central Valley in California; volcanic peaks (Mt. Rainier, Mt. Hood, Mt. Shasta) visible from many inland roads.
nature.climate_signature: Mediterranean climate in California — dry golden hills much of the year, green only in winter/spring; markedly wetter, greyer, and more consistently green in Oregon/Washington ('Pacific Northwest drizzle' look).

vehicles.plate_color: California: white plate with red/blue script and yellow DMV lettering; Oregon: white/blue with a tree silhouette; Washington: white plate with a green mountain silhouette.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Noticeably higher EV/Tesla presence than the national average, especially in California; logging trucks common on rural Oregon/Washington roads.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Mix of generations; very dense, frequently updated Gen 3/4 coverage in and around the Bay Area, LA, Seattle and Portland.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Some of the best and most current coverage in the country given tech-industry proximity; still has real gaps in remote redwood-country and Cascade mountain roads.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same Pacific coastal conifer forest (Douglas fir, cedar, hemlock), similar mountainous terrain and grey drizzly climate in Washington/BC
confusion_set.tiebreaker: US plates carry a state name with yellow center lines and mph signage; Canadian BC plates and km/h signage, plus French appearing on some federally-mandated packaging/signage, mark the Canadian side.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country, some shared conifer forest at elevation inland
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The Pacific region has redwoods, a Pacific coastline and Mediterranean/marine climate; the Mountain West has red-rock desert, sagebrush and a drier, higher-elevation look with no ocean coastline.
